people.name: Roscoe Whitfield
people.role: a bootlegger with the lease on the top floor

people.name: Alonzo Colquitt
people.relationshipToVictim: a childhood friend of the victim’s from the same block

secret.label: Fencing stolen goods
secret.description: Colquitt hands a parcel of stolen goods to a man at Ruggiero’s from 8:30 PM.

secret.label: Murder
secret.description: Vogel is at the roof from 8:30 PM, alone with Whitfield when it happens at 8:30 PM.

motive.description: blamed the victim for a ruin

people.name: Augustus Dandridge
people.relationshipToVictim: a witness against the people the victim worked for

secret.label: Blackmailing the victim
secret.description: Dandridge meets the victim alone at the Hallam from 7:30 PM and asks for money.

people.name: Filomena Vitale
people.relationshipToVictim: the victim’s neighbour across the airshaft

secret.label: A child boarded out
secret.description: Vitale goes to the ferry slip from 10:30 PM to see a child nobody is supposed to know about.

secret.label: Fencing stolen goods
secret.description: Sweeney hands a parcel of stolen goods to a man at Ruggiero’s from 8:30 PM.

people.name: Teresa Marchetti
people.role: a widow with rooms on the avenue

secret.label: Drinking in secret
secret.description: Marchetti drinks alone at Dolan’s from 8:00 PM to 8:30 PM and will claim to have been anywhere else.

method.name: a gunshot
method.bodyEvidence: One bullet below the sternum. Powder burns on the shirt front: fired close.

anchors.name: the regular who takes the same seat every night

traces.description: the regular was drinking sherry, and said twice what he thought of the beer

anchors.timing: when the regular came in for his seat
anchors.highTiming: as the regular was settling on his stool
anchors.sceneFact: The regular took his stool at {T}, which is the hour he takes it six nights a week.

anchors.name: the bells at St. Malachy’s

traces.description: the half hours are rung and the whole hours are rung twice

anchors.sceneFact: The bells rang the half hour at {T}. The sexton rings them off the sacristy clock and it keeps good time.

anchors.name: the beat cop’s pass
anchors.highTiming: as the cop was coming round
anchors.sceneFact: The patrolman’s round brought him two streets off at {T}.

Whitfield was found at the roof. The cigarette he had going burned itself out on the sill where it fell. The bells rang the half hour at 8:30 PM. The sexton rings them off the sacristy clock and it keeps good time.
The coroner puts death between 7:30 PM and 9:00 PM — two hours of nothing useful. One bullet below the sternum. Powder burns on the shirt front: fired close.
A nickel-plated revolver is gone from the fourth floor. The drawer it was kept in is open and the oiled cloth is still in it.
Ruggiero puts Whitfield at Ruggiero’s when the regular came in for his seat, which was 8:00 PM, and alive enough to argue about the weather.
Dandridge was at Dolan’s at 8:30 PM and heard a shot from the direction of the roof, while the bells were going.
Vitale was at Dolan’s at 8:30 PM and heard a shot from the direction of the roof, while the bells were going.

Found at the fourth floor: A clipping about the failure of Vogel’s business, with Whitfield’s name underlined twice in pencil.
Thorndike says Vogel said Whitfield had taken everything and would be made to feel it.
Found at the fourth floor: A subpoena naming Whitfield before the grand jury, with Dandridge’s name written in the margin.
Ruggiero says Whitfield said to Dandridge that a man who testifies sleeps better.
Found at the roof: A promissory note for $4,000 signed by Sweeney, endorsed to Whitfield, three months past due.
Vogel says Whitfield told Sweeney that Friday was the end of it, one way or the other.
Found at Ruggiero’s: A draft codicil in Whitfield’s hand striking Marchetti out of the will, dated last Tuesday and unsigned.
Thorndike says Whitfield told Marchetti the lawyer was coming Thursday and that the arrangement would be changed.
Vitale hired us, and wants it known that Vogel blamed the victim for a ruin, and would rather we started there.
Thorndike on Colquitt: Colquitt was carrying a parcel into Ruggiero’s and came out without it.
Ruggiero on Colquitt: There is a man who meets people at Ruggiero’s and nobody will say his name out loud.
Dandridge on Colquitt: Colquitt has been selling things that were never Colquitt’s to sell.
Wrapping paper and a cut string at Ruggiero’s, and the shop it came from closed two years ago.
A pawn ticket at Ruggiero’s in a name that does not exist, made out at the hour in question.
The receiver at Ruggiero’s would rather talk than be held: Colquitt was there from 8:30 PM handing over a parcel of somebody else’s silver, which is a charge Colquitt will take over this one.
The goods turn up, tagged and dated, and the tag puts Colquitt at Ruggiero’s from 8:30 PM with both hands full.
Sweeney on Dandridge: Dandridge and the victim were heard at the Hallam, and one of them was doing all the talking.
Thorndike on Dandridge: Dandridge has come into money lately and has no visible way of having come into money.
Ruggiero on Dandridge: The victim had been drawing cash in amounts that did not match anything in the accounts.
An envelope at the Hallam with nothing in it, addressed in the victim’s hand to no one.
A photograph at the Hallam, folded small, of something the victim would have paid to keep folded.
The victim’s bank book settles it: four payments, and Dandridge at the Hallam from 7:30 PM collecting the fifth. It is extortion, and an extortionist wants the man alive.
The thing Dandridge was holding over the victim turns up, and it was worth more to Dandridge every month than once.
Vogel on Vitale: Vitale sends money out of every pay envelope and cannot say where it goes.
Sweeney on Vitale: A woman at the ferry slip asked for Vitale by a name Vitale has not used in years.
Thorndike on Vitale: Vitale keeps a photograph and will not be asked about it twice.
A board-and-keep receipt at the ferry slip, monthly, eight years of them.
A child’s shoe at the ferry slip, and nobody at the ferry slip has any children.
The woman who keeps the child says it straight out: Vitale was at the ferry slip from 10:30 PM, the same as every week, and left with the same face as always.
The parish register at the ferry slip has the christening in it, and the board money receipted through the evening in question.

Dandridge on Marchetti: Marchetti had taken a drink and had gone to some trouble about the smell of it.
Thorndike on Marchetti: Marchetti is on a temperance pledge that Marchetti mentions before anybody asks.
Ruggiero on Marchetti: Somebody at Dolan’s says Marchetti is in more often than Marchetti lets on.
A bottle at Dolan’s pushed behind the pipes, the seal broken and the level down.
A tab at Dolan’s in a name that is not Marchetti’s, in Marchetti’s handwriting.
The man behind the counter at Dolan’s knows exactly: Marchetti was on the same stool from 8:00 PM to 8:30 PM and was in no condition to walk anywhere, let alone do this.
The tab at Dolan’s is dated and timed, from 8:00 PM to 8:30 PM, and Marchetti was there to run it up.
